2. Official self-hosted Bitwarden — https://bitwarden.com/help/hosting-faqs/
This offers the same required client family with an official server deployed in Docker containers. Its security whitepaper explains that the client sends a derived master-password authentication hash to its server, which salts and hashes it again; vault decryption happens on the client (https://bitwarden.com/help/bitwarden-security-white-paper/). With a correctly configured self-hosted installation, that server is yours. However, standard deployments can contact external services for updates, push notifications and certain account features. The FAQ points to offline deployment for preventing those outbound connections and explains the installation ID/key used for registration, push and paid-feature licensing. Choose that deployment model if eliminating service dependencies is essential, and distinguish an external licensing or update contact from sending your vault authentication hash to an external vault service.

**SDL2 is my second choice, and the more relevant choice if your main concern is avoiding a hard link to one particular display-server library.** For a simple software-surface path, create a window with `SDL_CreateWindow()`, get its surface with `SDL_GetWindowSurface()`, fill the surface using its actual pixel format and stride, and call `SDL_UpdateWindowSurface()`. The surface must be reacquired after a resize, and this surface path cannot be mixed with SDL's renderer or 3D API on the same window. You need not write OpenGL or Vulkan rendering code for this route. [Window creation](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2/SDL_CreateWindow), [window surface](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2/SDL_GetWindowSurface), [presenting the surface](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL2/SDL_UpdateWindowSurface)
